content.text: The best running shoe is the one that fits your foot shape, gait pattern, and running goals. There is no single universally best shoe — what works perfectly for one runner may cause injury in another.
How to Choose a Running Shoe

items: Visit a specialty running store for a gait analysis
Consider pronation type: neutral, overpronation, or supination
Match cushioning to your training: high-mileage needs more cushion
Ensure a thumb-width of space in the toe box
Try shoes in the evening when feet are slightly larger

content.text: The Brooks Ghost 16 remains our top pick for everyday training. Its DNA Loft v3 cushioning is both plush and responsive, the fit is consistent across widths, and the durability is exceptional — most runners get 400–500 miles before replacement.

items.question: How often should I replace running shoes?
items.answer: Most running shoes last 300–500 miles. Signs it is time to replace: loss of cushioning responsiveness, visible midsole compression, upper wear, or increased aches in your feet, knees, or hips after runs.

items.question: Do I need a specific running shoe if I walk more than run?
items.answer: Yes. Walking places different stress on the foot than running. Walking shoes are flatter and more flexible at the ball of the foot. If you do both, a neutral running shoe with moderate cushioning works well for either activity.
